title: The JavaScript Workshop
notes: The workshop turns a list of language features into a sequence of working programs. Start with values and small functions, then trace what happens when your code shares data, calls another operation, or waits for a result. Every lesson pairs a runnable example with a check for understanding and a challenge you can implement.

prompts.title: GM checkpoint
prompts.body: Given const badge = { visits: 1 }, what happens when you run badge.visits += 1?

options.text: The program throws because badge uses const.
The property changes to 2 and badge still refers to the same object.

title: Comparisons and Defaults
notes: Predict strict equality, boolean conditions and nullish defaults.
Use strict equality for comparisons and choose a default based on what counts as missing.

prompts.title: Listing 2.1 scratchpad
prompts.body: Predict the output. Then change one input and explain the result.
prompts.starter:
const savedVolume = 0;
const retryLimit = undefined;
console.log(savedVolume || 50); // 50
console.log(savedVolume ?? 50); // 0
console.log(retryLimit ?? 3); // 3
console.log('7' === 7, Number('7') === 7); // false true
console.log(Number.isFinite(Number('oops'))); // false
prompts.feedback: Your code draft is saved.

title: Comparisons and Defaults

prompts.title: GM checkpoint
prompts.body: A user sets volume to 0. Which expression preserves that setting and defaults to 50 for null or undefined?

options.text: volume || 50
Boolean(volume) ? volume : 50
volume ?? 50
volume === 0 ? 50 : volume

prompts.feedback: Zero is falsy but is neither null nor undefined. The nullish operator preserves it.

prompts.title: GM checkpoint
prompts.body: Where should the worker advance the shared cursor?

options.text: After awaiting work so other workers see the same current position.
Before awaiting work, when it claims the position.
Only after the entire pool has completed.
In a timer callback shared by all workers.

prompts.feedback: Claim and advance in a synchronous step. After an await, another worker may have observed the old position.
